standard.title: IEC 62304 — software life cycle processes, mapped by clause title only
standard.scope_note: The standard text is paid (CHF 1,150 for the consolidated version). Only the table of contents - clause numbers and titles - is public, and that is all this file quotes. Every row therefore carries verbatim=false and may be PARTIAL or GAP, never carried: a clause whose requirement text nobody on this project has read cannot be claimed as covered. Five clauses, chosen because a record layer might plausibly touch them; the other thirty-five are not listed, which is itself the answer.

rows.reason: Class A/B/C is assigned from the device risk analysis and drives which tasks are mandatory. This is a decision about the product, made by the manufacturer against ISO 14971; a record layer has nothing to classify and cannot answer it.

A released package names every artefact by digest and seals the set, so the released thing is identifiable and a later edit is detectable. What is missing: the release decision itself - who approved it, against which verification results, and whether every required task for the assigned safety class was actually performed.

The seal makes an uncontrolled change visible: alter a byte and verification stops agreeing with the manifest. That is detection, not control - approval of a change, impact analysis and re-baselining stay in the manufacturer's configuration management process.

rows.id: IEC 62304 7.1 Analysis of software contributing to hazardous situations
rows.reason: This is engineering analysis: which software functions can contribute to which hazardous situations. Nothing in a record layer performs it, and a placeholder table of hazards would be worse than an acknowledged gap.

Problem and change events are appended with identity and time and can be read back in one command. What is missing: the content requirements of the records (who investigated, what was concluded, which verification closed it) and retention rules.
